_help: Read by study_brief.py at import; restart the tray after editing.

modules: names, codes and aliases for each module. Modules with a dated Coursework.md in the vault are found at runtime as well (their name and code become keys automatically); entries here only add aliases and fix the order she lists them in.

matching: how a module is recognised. 1) any alias, the full name or the code as whole words; 2) word prefixes in order ('sig and sys', 'comp meth'), each at least min_prefix letters (min_prefix_alone when the name is one word), connectors skipped; 3) a near-miss spelling of an alias ('signls'). The first tier that names exactly one module wins; two modules in one tier = none.
patterns: regexes with inline flags. Keep their capture groups. {heading}, {week} and {n} are filled at runtime (regex-escaped); no other braces are formatted.

templates: Python format strings. Date fields take strftime specs, e.g. {due:%a %d %b %Y}. Entries with 'one'/'many' are picked by count. verify_due must produce the same text as the due date in brief.due.

learner.format_first: one rule per kind of format belief. pattern = what the claim names (the earliest-named kind wins); shape = the adaptation it calls for, or null for none; revise_first (optional) = a regex for the revise-from sources moved to the front. A new shape needs its intro lines at templates.brief.<shape> and its footer line at templates.brief.shaped.<shape>; the footer lists adaptations in templates.brief.shaped order.

templates.which_module: Which module is the study brief for?
templates.submit_step: Assemble, check and submit on KEATS

brief.source: > From [[{link}|the coursework note]]. Built {today:%d %b} from your notes only.
brief.source_undated: > Built {today:%d %b} from your week notes only — no coursework note found.
brief.nothing_planned: Nothing to plan yet: every week note is written up and there's no coursework listed.
brief.brief_unread: - **The brief isn't read yet** — the plan below is guessed from the deadline until it is.
example_first: Start each item from a worked example (tutorial sheet or past paper), then the theory it uses.
diagram_first: Start each item from a sketch or diagram of the problem, then the theory it uses.
